>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump is pledging to send a one-time payment of $90 to seniors
to help them pay their Medicare premiums.
NPR's Frank Langford reports the cost of living remains a major issue
for voters just five weeks before the midterm elections.
>> Trump announced Friday the checks would go to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees.
In a video, he said the money would arrive soon in people's bank accounts.
>> You'll get your money almost immediately.
In everything we do, we're looking out for America's people and America's seniors

>> Trump said he'll use money from the government's Medicare Improvement Fund.

to improve the original Medicare program.
Last month, Trump promised American adults $5,000 each
if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms.
Polls in recent weeks show 60% of those polled disapprove of the job Trump's doing.
Frank Langford, NPR News, Washington.
>> U.S. business owners say rising diesel costs are putting pressure on their bottom line.
G7 nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel
from the reserves in hopes of easing prices.
Mark St. Clair owns a pool cleaning company in Sandusky, Ohio.
>> We do so many calls a day.
You know, these trucks are on the road six days a week,
and it's just our costs are going up, up, up.
And it's almost to the point where we've got to raise all of our prices to the customers.
>> According to AAA, the national average for diesel today is $6.34 a gallon.
The U.S. Coast Guard says it's located a debris field off the coast of Nantucket
from a Canadian air ambulance.
Shortly before the plane went missing,
the pilot had tried to communicate with air traffic control.
>> Copy. One zero four, madam I go.
Pay the grand emergency and this one one four.
>> Paul Connery from member station WBUR reports
the plane was carrying six people from Bermuda to Boston.
>> The four Canadian crew members in two Bermudian nationals
were headed to Logan Airport after taking off
from Bermuda's LF Wade International Airport.
The plane was south of Nantucket at 1 a.m. local time
when the pilot reported trouble.
The Coast Guard says the pilot told air traffic control
that the aircraft was having electrical problems
and declared an emergency.
Radio transmissions indicate that the Gulf Stream
G100 may have been coming in blind,
indicating the aircraft may have lost its navigational instruments
just as a storm moved across its path on radar.
The air ambulance jet was registered to a Canadian company
that transports patients.
For NPR News, I'm Paul Connery in Boston.
>> This is NPR News.
President Trump has posted Senator Tom Cotton's personal cell phone number online,
urging people to call the Arkansas Republican
over his opposition to permanent daylight saving time.
Trump wants the Senate to pass the Sunshine Protection Act,
which cleared the House in July.
Cotton is among the Republican senators who oppose it.
Trump argued yesterday that the change would give Americans
more daylight when they're most active.
Cotton says it would make winter a "dark and dismal time."
A large gray shark has captivated the attention of people in South Korea.
Authorities are trying to free the animal from a canal
where it's been stuck for more than two weeks.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul.
>> The 11-and-a-half-foot-long gray shark has been named Bukangi
after the North Port Park in the port city of Busan where he's stuck.
Authorities have used jets of water and nets
to try to coax Bukangi back out to sea,
but the shark has so far ignored or dodged them all.
Over half a million people have come to see him.
He's gone viral on social media,
and last week the city officially appointed him as an honorary ambassador.
While tourists are entertained by Bukangi,
there is concern about his health if he remains trapped in the canal.
And environmental activists and marine biologists
say Bukangi's presence may be a warning sign
that warming seas are driving marine life north.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
